name: Double A-Gap Mad Dog Overload
formation: 46 Mad Dog vs Gun 21 Personnel 2x1 Right

summary.motive: Overload both A-gaps with walked defenders so the offense’s pass-protection slide cannot account for every interior threat, forcing an instant-pressure throw or sack.
summary.keyDefender: SS mugged over the strong A-gap — the blocker assigned to him cannot get depth fast enough
summary.whyItWorks: A single running back can pick up only one of the two A-gap knives, and the head-up end slant removes the tackle’s ability to help either guard.
summary.failureMode: A quick perimeter throw (slant/flat) released on time beats the press corner before the interior knives arrive.

beats.title: 1. The Mad Dog Picture
beats.text: WILL and the strong safety stand mugged directly over both A-gaps at 1.2 yards with corners pressing outside. The offense must account for five immediate threats with only six protectors.

beats.title: 2. Same-Gap Knives
beats.text: Both A-gap defenders cross the guards’ inside shoulders simultaneously while the head-up end slants hard off the tight end. The center-guard doubles are left blocking air.

beats.title: 3. Hot Window Slams Shut
beats.text: The QB’s hot slant to X was the escape valve, but the island press corner rides it upfield while the safety blitz arrives before the third step lands.

beats.title: 4. Buried Between Both Gaps
beats.text: The NOSE has driven the center into the QB’s lap and the slanting end closes the scramble lane. Six rushers versus five blockers plus a scanning back ends one way.

relations.tell: Both A-gap defenders are standing upright at 1.2 yards staring across the line pre-snap — the base 46 keeps its safeties at 5 and 8 yards instead.
